I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and maize here, and I've done the same for forty years. The soil is familiar to me — sandy loam, not the best, but I know how much water it needs and when.

My land is about 10 mu. All of it goes into the wheat-maize rotation. I wouldn't change that now. At my age I'm not going to experiment. The wheat is already in the ground from last October — I planted Jimai 22, same as the last several years. It yields well and the seed station carries it. For the maize coming up after wheat harvest in June, I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed. Every farmer around here uses it. It's reliable.

For wheat I water four times — the pre-winter water in November is essential, then jointing, heading, and one more at grain filling if it's dry. This year I'll try to cut one irrigation if rain helps, because the well level has dropped again and pumping costs more. But I won't risk the crop.

Fertilizer — I apply a base dressing before wheat planting, diammonium phosphate and urea, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. For maize I put fertilizer down at planting and again when the plant is knee-high. I spray herbicide once early and watch for aphids and borer on maize.

I use rotary tillage before wheat. For maize I seed directly into the wheat stubble — saves time and the machine does it in a day.
